_comment: DanceSafe reagent testing flowcharts, transcribed by hand.
Source: DanceSafe 'DC_Testing_Flows' 2023 V1.3, charts 1, 2 (sides 1 and 2)
and 3. Hand-transcribed from the published charts rather than generated,
because DanceSafe publishes them as artwork and there is no data feed.
WHY THIS EXISTS SEPARATELY FROM reagents.json. That file is one row per
substance per reagent: what color, independent of every other reagent. It
is a lookup table and it is generated, and its header forbids hand-edits.
A flowchart is a different claim and a stronger one: run THESE reagents in
THIS ORDER, and this specific sequence of colors is what the substance is
expected to produce. That is how a reagent test is actually run, and it is
the difference between 'black is one of the colors Marquis gives for MDMA'
and 'black then royal blue is the MDMA result'.
COLORS ARE MOSTLY THE PICKER'S PLAIN BUCKETS, widened from what DanceSafe
writes — royal blue and bright blue and ice blue are all `blue` — because a
spot plate under a kitchen light is not a laboratory, and widening can only
cost precision where narrowing could eliminate the substance somebody is
holding. The chart's own wording is kept in `says` for display.
THREE EXCEPTIONS, and they are exceptions because the charts FORK on them.
peach goes to Morris and toward cocaine while bright orange goes to
Liebermann and toward amphetamine; magenta is heroin's Marquis and sits
between the pink that opens the cocaine branch and purple; olive is 2C-B's
dark lime green. A color the chart forks on has to be one the reader can
say, so the picker offers all three and reagentmatch.js maps each back to
the table words it falls between for the 207-substance scoring.
steps[] is ordered. `colors` are the accepted readings at that step,
`none: true` means no reaction is accepted, and both may be set.

_comment: Chart 3, TESTING UNKNOWN SUBSTANCES. A router rather than a flow: it has
no endpoint of its own, it reads a Marquis and sends you to one of the
tests above, which is why it is shaped differently from `flows`.
PEACH IS ITS OWN COLOR HERE, and getting that wrong broke the router.
The chart separates PEACH and LIGHT PINK, which go to Morris and toward
cocaine, from BRIGHT ORANGE, which goes to Liebermann and toward
amphetamine, meth or mescaline. Folding peach into `orange` merged the
two branches: an orange Marquis then offered Morris, listed cocaine as
live, and could finish BOTH the cocaine and the methamphetamine
sequences off one reading. The picker offers peach as its own choice now
rather than making somebody round it to a branch.
`next` is the reagent the chart says to run SECOND — one step, not the
whole branch. `then` is the step after that, keyed on what the second
reagent did, because that is where chart 3 hands off to charts 1 and 2:
a light-yellow Liebermann goes to the amphetamine/meth test at Simon's,
a yellow-brown one goes to the mescaline test at Froehde. Without it a
Liebermann reading could not narrow anything, since neither the meth nor
the amphetamine flow has a Liebermann step to contradict.

unknownRule: Any Marquis result the charts do not list should be treated as an unexpected reaction for a ground score or mystery substance. Without context around what something was sold as, further differentiation may be misleading.
